terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Approximate anterior matched-view camera for an uncalibrated vision-context set; not a clinical or solved pose.

materialFamilies: mixed satin and semi-gloss organic surfaces
objectClass.notes: Five uncalibrated workflow views show one stylized external heart. Reconstruct the shared macro/meso structure and treat tiny single-view coronary details as conditional. This is an object-domain teaching prop, not a humanoid character and not diagnostic anatomy.

reasoning: The silhouette is organically interrupted by multiple great-vessel openings, an aortic arch and asymmetric atrial/fat masses.
The component hierarchy includes a continuous ventricular body, atrial complex, multiple branching vessel systems, a surface coronary network and repeated fat lobules.
Five views constrain the shared volume but create high occlusion risk around vessel roots and posterior return paths.
Identity depends on macro proportions, meso topology and dense but bounded surface-attached vessel detail, justifying ultra-complex depth.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The five-view reconstruction needs separate macro, meso and micro contracts: continuous myocardium, attached great-vessel topology, repeated lobulated fat, hierarchical coronary curves, material zones and five critical matched viewpoints.

details.description: Ventricular body tapers to an inferior apex offset toward subject-left/anterior.
Right-ventricular volume wraps the anterior wall with a shallow interventricular transition.
Broad superior atrioventricular groove receives fat pads and coronary trunks.
Wide aortic root sweeps posteriorly into a thick arch with a stable inner negative space.
Exactly three separated superior arch branches terminate in thick-walled hollow openings.
Pulmonary trunk crosses anterior to the aortic root before lateral bifurcation.
Bilateral pulmonary branches keep visible wall thickness and recessed lumens.
Caval paths connect to the right-atrial region and retain hollow superior/inferior openings where visible.
Paired lateral return tubes enter the posterior atrial complex without floating roots.
Broad irregular pale lobules overlap the subject-left atrial/AV region with varied size and overlap.
Smaller asymmetric pale lobules overlap the subject-right atrial/AV region.
Posterior epicardial fat forms a broad irregular cap, not a uniform bead ring.
Red arterial and dark burgundy venous trunks descend along anterior grooves and branch hierarchically.
Coronary paths stay flush while wrapping both lateral ventricular walls.
Sparse posterior coronary paths continue from the sides and taper instead of disappearing abruptly.
Low-frequency organic undulation and sparse directional fiber ridges remain subordinate to the ventricular volume.
Great vessels are smoother than myocardium; fat has broad wet-satin highlights without global mirror response.
Colored hotspot rings, beige background, pedestal, upper-right UI and text are excluded rather than mapped to any model surface.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedLimitations: Hidden internal anatomy is outside the external-model scope.
Camera labels remain approximate workflow viewpoints.
Unsupported low-resolution micro branches are omitted rather than hallucinated.
Occluded return-vessel roots use cross-view-consistent stylized routing.
PBR values are visual estimates and do not claim physical tissue measurement.
All hotspot rings, background, pedestal, UI and text are excluded from implementation.

definitionOfDone: One coherent procedural THREE.Group reproduces the five-view asymmetric ventricular silhouette, superior vessel topology, atrial/fat coverage and continuous coronary network without using downloaded meshes or billboards.

The ascending aorta, arch and exactly three superior branches; pulmonary trunk and bilateral branches; vena-cava and visible pulmonary-return paths are rooted, non-floating and have visibly hollow cut ends.
Five critical matched renders named anterior, left-oblique, posterior, right-oblique and superior each reach aiVisionScore >= 0.80 before continue.

Myocardium, arterial, venous, coronary and fat materials retain distinct reference-observed PBR response under neutral and grazing lighting without baking hotspots, background, pedestal or UI into the model.
The model remains clickable and explodable by semantic groups, passes strict spec validation, deterministic render diagnostics, multi-angle checks, pass gating and part coverage.

featureGroups.name: Five-view ventricular and atrial silhouette
qualityCriteria: The ventricular body is asymmetric, broad at the superior third and continuously tapered to an offset inferior apex.
Anterior, posterior, both oblique and superior silhouettes use one shared volume and preserve atrial overlap rather than view-specific local cheats.
failureModes: ventricular body reads as a symmetric ellipsoid or sphere pair
apex direction conflicts between front and oblique views
posterior body lacks the broad atrial/fat cap

featureGroups.name: Great-vessel topology and hollow openings
qualityCriteria: Aortic root, arch and exactly three superior branches form a continuous rooted sweep.
Pulmonary trunk crosses anterior to the aortic root and bifurcates laterally.
Vena-cava and visible pulmonary-return tubes enter the atrial complex with wall thickness and recessed lumens.
failureModes: visible vessel opening is closed by a solid cap
tube root floats or ends inside empty space
aortic branch count or front/back ordering conflicts with the superior view

featureGroups.name: Continuous surface-attached coronary network
qualityCriteria: Red arterial and dark burgundy venous trunks follow AV/interventricular grooves, branch hierarchically and wrap to lateral/posterior surfaces.
Every coronary curve keeps bounded embed depth against the myocardium and terminates by tapering or joining another visible path.
failureModes: coronary segment visibly floats above the muscle
coronary segment penetrates through the myocardium
side or posterior network disappears abruptly
micro branches are invented from a single blurred cue

featureGroups.name: Asymmetric atrial and epicardial fat coverage
qualityCriteria: Subject-left and subject-right atrial/auricular masses are unequal and partly hidden by distinct lobulated fat pads.
Fat lobules vary in scale, orientation and overlap while remaining embedded in the atrioventricular region.
Posterior coverage forms a broad irregular cap instead of a uniform ring of beads.
failureModes: atria are represented as symmetric spheres
fat becomes a uniform pearl necklace
fat lobes float above or form an implausible hard seam against the atria

featureGroups.name: Tissue material separation and bounded surface relief
qualityCriteria: Myocardium, arterial tubes, venous tubes, coronary vessels and fat use separate albedo/roughness responses grounded in visible tissue crops.
Myocardium has low-frequency volume undulation, sparse shallow directional grooves and restrained meso relief; no high-frequency noise blanket.
Neutral, grazing and matched lighting show broad semi-gloss highlights without turning all regions into the same plastic material.
failureModes: all tissue shares one global mirror-like material
reference highlights or colored hotspots are painted into albedo
surface noise obscures the macro heart form
arterial, venous and fat regions lose their reference-observed color separation

visualDeltaChecks: five-view ventricular silhouette, apex direction and atrial-overlap delta
aortic arch, three-branch, pulmonary-crossing and posterior-return topology delta
hollow vessel-opening count, wall-thickness and depth-ordering delta
left/right/posterior fat-lobule coverage and irregularity delta
anterior/lateral/posterior coronary continuity, embed depth and branch-density delta
myocardium/artery/vein/fat albedo, roughness and bounded-relief delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Adjacent components must overlap by at least 0.02 world units at shared seams (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Raised or recessed relief and fasteners must be geometry, instanced micro-parts, or displacement; a map alone is an approximation (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs view-matched reference/render screenshot pairs, one comparison sheet and AI vision score per gating source view, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Asymmetric ventricular/atrial silhouette and offset apex
Aortic arch/three branches, pulmonary crossing and posterior return paths
Surface-attached artery/vein network across anterior, lateral and posterior walls
Asymmetric lobulated epicardial fat coverage and tissue material separation

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

Colored rings, background, pedestal, UI and text are not part of the heart.

proceduralStrategy: Lock one coordinate frame and five approximate review cameras before local detail.
Use a seam-free asymmetric implicit/tapered ventricular body for the macro silhouette.
Use thick curve/tube sweeps with recessed lumen inserts for all visible great-vessel openings.
Use hierarchical surface-conforming tube curves for coronary arteries and veins with bounded embed depth.
Use irregular clustered organic lobules for epicardial fat instead of a uniform bead ring.
Use independent region PBR channels and bounded low-frequency tissue relief; do not project source pixels.
Expose semantic groups, pivots, sockets and stable names for clicking, isolation and explosion views.
animationAnchors: ventricular-body root pivot supports whole-object transforms
macro semantic groups expose stable pivots for exploded-view separation
great-vessel and coronary groups retain named roots for optional pulse/deformation experiments
destructionAnchors: semantic tissue/vessel/fat groups can detach only in explicit exploded-view mode
no random fracture or internal anatomy is implied by the external teaching model
risks: Uncalibrated viewpoints make exact clinical camera and dimensions unavailable; matched cameras are approximate.
Low-resolution source views cap trustworthy tertiary coronary detail.
Dense curve/tube networks can exceed draw-call budget without geometry merging or instancing.
